meta.description: AER analysis: AerCap pairs six straight earnings beats, a raised $16.80 EPS guide and a $1.4B year-to-date buyback with one problem: the C-suite sold $18M of stock into the rally. A-, buy the pullback, not the high.
meta.ogDescription: AerCap at 8.5x forward earnings with six straight beats and a raised guide. Why we wait for 150 instead of chasing 155.

verdict.summary: AerCap is the world's largest aircraft lessor at 8.5x forward earnings, and it keeps doing the two things the market pays for: beating estimates (six consecutive quarters, the July 29 print by 30%) and shrinking the share count ($1.4B repurchased year to date). Management raised full-year EPS guidance to roughly $16.80 at the last report. The aircraft shortage does the heavy lifting: lease rates keep repricing higher while the order book is sold out for years. Two things keep this at A- instead of A+. First, the stock sits within 1% of its 52-week high, so a fresh buyer at 155 risks more to a sensible stop than the next resistance offers. Second, the insider tape is loud: fourteen sales and zero buys in ninety days, including the CFO ($11M), the CEO ($7.4M) and a chief accounting officer who sold every directly held share in June (a trust-held balance remains); all before the earnings pop, though part of the spring activity traces to routine RSU vesting rather than discretionary exits. The trade is to let the price come to you at the 150 zone, where the risk/reward flips above 3:1.

Aircraft scarcity supports lease-rate repricing for years — the order book is effectively sold out
Beta 0.93 and 0.8% short interest: a calm, under-shorted compounder
whyAvoid: Insider distribution into strength: 14 sales, 0 buys in 90 days: CFO $11M, CEO $7.4M, and the chief accounting officer sold all his directly held shares on June 15 (a trust-held balance remains)
0.7% below the 52-week high: at-market risk/reward is poor until a pullback or a confirmed breakout
AerCap raises guidance almost every quarter; the raise is partly expected, so its signal value is lower than it looks
Options positioning flags a bearish put/call tilt on the name
The customers are airlines: an oil shock or recession stresses lessee credit first — AerCap wrote off roughly $2.7B on its Russia fleet in 2022 (later partly recovered via insurance)
$43.1B of debt against $1.5B cash is the leasing model working as designed, but it makes the equity rate-sensitive

business.overview: AerCap owns and leases roughly two thousand aircraft plus engines and helicopters, buying them in bulk from Airbus and Boeing and renting them to airlines worldwide. The June quarter delivered $726M of net income ($4.59 per share) and $811M adjusted ($5.14), with revenue of $2.17B. Book value per share reached $119.21 at June 30, up about 16% in a year, and management keeps buying back stock below 1.4x that book value, which mechanically compounds per-share value. The aircraft shortage caused by delivery delays at both airframers keeps used-aircraft values and lease rates firm, which is why gains on sale keep landing above book.
business.moat: Scale (largest order book in the industry), purchasing power with Airbus/Boeing, and a funding cost advantage over smaller lessors. In a shortage, whoever owns the aircraft sets the price.
business.theme: Aviation supply crunch — lease rates repricing higher through the decade's delivery backlog.

earnings.beatNote: Six consecutive beats verified back through Q1 2025 (the data service only shows four quarters; the older two were checked against the company's releases). The streak is powered by gains on aircraft sales above book value: recurring in a shortage, but lumpy by nature. Next report: October 28.

recentTransactions.value: Sold all directly held shares; a trust-held balance remains

insiders.signal: 14 sales, zero buys in 90 days, all executed below the current price and before the earnings pop. Executives selling ahead of a quarter they knew was strong is the single loudest bear argument in this file, the panel docked the setup for it, and it is the main reason this is an A- and not more.

capitalStructure.atm: None — no ATM program, no equity shelf takedowns in the last 12 months
capitalStructure.shareHistory: Aggressive net reduction: 4.9M shares retired in Q2 2026 alone, over $1.4B repurchased year to date under an active $1B-tranche authorization

shortInterest.trend: Negligible and stable: no bear case is being expressed through the borrow. No squeeze story either.

technicals.setupNote: A clean four-week base between 144.07 and 156.33 sits on top of a rising EMA stack (149.94 > 146.94 > 138.14, MACD positive). The 52-week high was printed on earnings day (July 29) and faded to 148.63 before the price climbed back to the top of the range. That is constructive; but at 155.30 the stock trades 3.6% above its EMA20 with the ceiling 0.7% away. The two clean triggers: a pullback that holds the 149.5-150.5 zone (EMA20), or a confirmed daily close above 156.50 on volume.

macro.regime: Risk-on (VIX 15.9, SPX above all major averages). ISM services Aug 5 and the July jobs report Aug 7 are the near-term catalysts.
macro.impact: A hot jobs number pressuring rates is the macro risk that matters here: AerCap funds a $43B balance sheet, so its equity is rate-sensitive even at beta 0.93. The aircraft-shortage thesis itself is macro-resistant, airlines lease when they cannot buy.

risks.riskSummary: No dilution, no debt-wall, no binary event in the window. The risks are softer: an insider tape that says the people who know the company best took profits before the print, a guidance-raise habit that mutes each new raise, and the rate sensitivity that comes with a leased balance sheet.

riskCards.title: Insider Distribution Into Strength
points: 14 sales / 0 buys in 90 days, concentrated in May-June at $143-150
CFO ~$11M, CEO ~$7.4M, chief accounting officer out entirely on June 15
All sales predate the July 29 beat — profit-taking, but from the best-informed seats
riskCards.verdict: Not a fraud signal: a valuation signal. When the C-suite trims at 145-150, paying 155 needs a better reason than momentum.

riskCards.title: Rate Sensitivity of a Leased Balance Sheet
points: $43.1B total debt vs $1.5B cash; normal for the model, but funding costs reprice with rates
A hot NFP or CPI print lifts the discount rate on a spread business
Lease-rate repricing lags funding-cost moves by quarters
riskCards.verdict: Manageable while the shortage keeps lease rates climbing faster than funding costs.

riskCards.title: Guidance-Raise Fatigue
points: AerCap has raised guidance at nearly every quarterly report since 2024
The market increasingly prices the next raise in advance
EPS quality leans on gains-on-sale, which are recurring but lumpy
riskCards.verdict: The raise is real money, but its surprise value decays, which is why the stock faded after printing the high on earnings day.

tradeIdea.statusNote: No chase at 155.30 with the 52-week high 0.7% away — the at-market risk/reward is close to 1:1. This is a limit-order setup: let the price come back to the entry zone, or pay up only on proof.
tradeIdea.entryNote: Scenario A (preferred): a pullback into 149.50-150.50: the EMA20 zone and the middle of the four-week base; that holds on the retest. Scenario B: a confirmed daily close above 156.50 on volume opens blue sky; take half size there with a stop under 150, and be honest that the math is thinner on that path.
tradeIdea.thesis: An 8.5x-earnings compounder with six straight beats, a raised guide and a shrinking share count deserves a position, at the right price. The panel's number is 150: there the stop tucks under the EMA50 at 1.5×ATR and the first target pays 3.3 times the risk.

globalScore.profile: A-, an elite operator at a cheap multiple, docked for insider distribution and an entry that has not come to you yet.

globalScore.mindsetTip: A great company at the wrong spot is a mediocre trade. The discipline is the limit order at 150; if it never fills, you lost nothing; if it fills, you own the dip everyone else chased.
